name: NVIDIA
next_event: Q3 FY2027 results, historically late November (not confirmed)
headline: Growth is re-accelerating at a $300B+ run rate, but NVIDIA is increasingly financing the buildout itself, and the stock is flat on the year.

takeaways.text: Revenue grew 106% YoY last quarter to $96.2B. YoY growth has risen for four straight quarters, from 56% to 106%.
Data Center was $89.0B, about 92% of revenue. Gross margin is about 75% and operating margin about 66%.
Cash is lagging profit: Q2 free cash flow was $21.4B against $59.7B of net income. DSO rose from 45 to 60 days on extended payment terms.
NVIDIA guaranteed up to $105B of OpenAI data center lease payments and committed $36B to rent cloud capacity back from partners.
At 25x trailing earnings, NVIDIA trades below Broadcom, TI and AMD. The market is not paying for current earnings; the thesis has to explain why.

business.text: Describes itself as a "data center scale AI infrastructure company": GPUs, Grace CPUs, NVLink and InfiniBand/Ethernet networking, full rack-scale systems, and the CUDA software stack.
Two segments: Compute & Networking (Data Center, Automotive) and Graphics (GeForce gaming, RTX workstations).
Within Data Center, Hyperscale was $48.7B (+102% YoY) and AI clouds, industrial & enterprise (ACIE) grew 138%.
One direct customer was 16% of Q2 revenue. In 1H, three direct customers were 16%, 15% and 13%. One AI lab contributed "a meaningful amount" indirectly through cloud providers.
Fabless: wafers from TSMC and Samsung, memory from SK Hynix, Micron and Samsung, assembly by Hon Hai, Wistron and Fabrinet. The supply chain is "mainly concentrated in Asia."
Named competitors: AMD, Intel, Huawei, Broadcom, and in-house chips at Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft.

why_it_matters: NVIDIA is now essentially a single-market company selling to a handful of very large buyers. The stock trades on hyperscaler and AI-lab spending plans more than on its own quarterly beats.

guidance.text: Q3 FY27 outlook: revenue $108.0B ±2% (about +12% QoQ, +89% YoY) and gross margin 74.0% ±50bp. Assumes no China Data Center compute revenue.

exposures.label: OpenAI lease guarantees (Ohio, ~4.25 GW)
exposures.note: Pays the shortfall if OpenAI defaults; payments expected from 2028

exposures.label: Cloud capacity bought back from partners
exposures.note: Typically 6-year commitments under the new AI cloud partner model

exposures.label: Accounts receivable
exposures.note: DSO 60 days, up from 45 one quarter earlier

exposures.label: Third-party AI financing platforms (MOUs)
exposures.note: Preliminary; NVIDIA may give limited residual-value support

events.text: Agreed to acquire Hugging Face for about $11.9B, plus up to $1.0B in retention equity.
Q2 FY27 results: revenue $96.2B, Q3 guide $108B. Vera Rubin began production shipments in Q3.
Residual value guarantees on OpenAI-tenanted data center leases with SB Energy, capped at $105B, with an option on about 3.8 GW more.
Hired Nicholas Parker, 26 years at Microsoft, as EVP Worldwide Field Operations.
FY2026 annual report: revenue $215.9B (+65%), including a $4.5B H20 inventory charge after China export rules changed.

debates.q: Is NVIDIA financing its own demand?
debates.detail: Lease guarantees, cloud buy-backs, longer payment terms and a $500B+ financing platform. How much revenue depends on NVIDIA's balance sheet, and what happens if a large AI lab can't pay?

debates.q: How long can customer spending last?
debates.detail: Growth depends on a few hyperscalers and AI labs. Their capex guidance and their own AI revenue are the leading indicators.

debates.q: Will custom chips cap share or margins?
debates.detail: Broadcom and Marvell build hyperscalers' in-house accelerators. Watch whether NVIDIA's 75% gross margin holds as those ramp.

debates.q: Are $279B of commitments confidence or inventory risk?
debates.detail: The FY26 $4.5B H20 charge showed how quickly commitments become write-downs when demand shifts.

debates.q: Is China an option or a zero?
debates.detail: Data Center China revenue is effectively zero and excluded from guidance. Any return is upside; the question is whether the market already assumes none.

questions: NVIDIA trades at 25x trailing earnings while growing 100%+. Is the market right to be skeptical? What would make 25x expensive?
Do the OpenAI guarantee and extended payment terms worry you, or are they normal for a dominant supplier? Compare Cisco and Lucent's vendor financing in 1999-2000.
Which single KPI would tell you whether the bull or bear case is winning: Data Center growth, gross margin, DSO and cash conversion, or customer concentration?

sources.label: 8-K Q2 results, press release and CFO commentary (2026-08-26)
